summary: Adds a /download endpoint that serves files from the upload directory by name, and switches the dev server to bind all interfaces with debug enabled.

findings.title: Path traversal in download endpoint
findings.description: The handler joins the raw name query parameter onto the upload directory and serves the result. os.path.join accepts ../ segments and discards the base when name is absolute. Any caller can read any file the server process can open, such as /etc/passwd or application secrets. Use safe_join from werkzeug, or resolve the path and verify it stays under UPLOAD_DIR, before calling send_file.

findings.fix: Use safe_join from werkzeug, or resolve the path and verify it stays under UPLOAD_DIR, before calling send_file.

findings.title: Werkzeug debugger enabled on all interfaces
findings.description: The app now runs with debug enabled, which exposes the interactive Werkzeug debugger on every exception. Combined with the all-interfaces bind, the debugger is reachable from the network. Anyone who can reach port 5000 can trigger an error page and run arbitrary Python on the host. Remove debug=True from app.run and read the debug setting from an environment variable such as FLASK_DEBUG for local use only.

findings.title: Dev server bound to all interfaces
findings.description: The host changed from loopback to 0.0.0.0, so the Flask development server accepts connections from any network interface. The previous binding limited it to the local machine. The unauthenticated download endpoint and the debugger become reachable by every host on the network. Restore host="127.0.0.1" or read the bind address from an environment variable so only deployments that need it opt in.

findings.title: New download endpoint has no test
findings.description: The change adds a download handler with a 404 branch and a file response. The repository contains no test files, so no test exercises either path. Regressions in the 404 handling or path validation will ship unnoticed. Add a test module that calls /download with a missing, valid, and traversal name. Assert the response for each case.
